serialization_protocol: Immediately before each append, re-scan the authoritative ledger for the proposed stable key and retrieve the current head of every declared parent and dependency.
Append exactly one OPEN event through the authorized operation; no concurrent or batch appender may act.
Read back and verify the exact event identity, stable key, state, content hash, parent/dependency bindings, and resulting authoritative head before considering the next event.

If any key collision, new head, stale revision, or verification mismatch appears, stop; do not append the next event; coordinate through the operator-designated Eddie Brock coordination hub and rebase plus re-review the affected draft.

items.title: TownSquare Working Default
items.goal: Make TownSquare the normal operator engagement, communication, audit, routing, and outcome interface while Drive becomes reconciled history and material actions remain exact-action governed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every supported operator engagement creates one immutable receipt with protected exact evidence and causal attribution before disposition returns.
Ordinary authenticated audit intake needs no per-message action permit; every material action fails without exact applicable authority and a safe permit trace.
Canonical Registry and Revere work is reconciled without duplicate replacement items and completes under its own accepted criteria.
Town Watch and approved clients use native TownSquare intake and Revere transport without Drive publication or manual prompt relay.
An independently verified release is restored in isolation and promoted to NAS only under exact authorization, with no unreconciled accepted Drive record.
The operator records independent acceptance; Crier visibility, message delivery, or implementer self-review is insufficient.

Under the controlling operator ruling, Eddie Brock is product owner for all ongoing projects and coordinates code freezes and assignments through the operator-designated Eddie Brock coordination hub, but cannot self-review, independently accept, issue permits by role alone, authorize deployment/rollback/cutover or external contact, or authorize probe cleanup. Any session-to-hub mapping exists only in protected Registry evidence, never in filing drafts or native events.

Authoritative filing is serialized by the one designated writer: immediately re-scan key and current parent/dependency heads before each append, append exactly one event, verify its exact event/head, and stop for hub-coordinated rebase and re-review on any collision, new head, stale revision, or mismatch.

items.title: Commit mandatory receipts, protected evidence, and causal trace
items.goal: Atomically receipt operator inputs, retain protected exact evidence, and link routing and outcomes without claiming cross-service atomicity.

acceptance_criteria.text: Statement, request, instruction, correction, approval, stop, malformed, rejected, and failed engagements each create exactly one immutable receipt under idempotent replay.

One local transaction commits event ID, safe receipt, protected exact bytes/digest, actor/session/lineage, causal links, routing/interpretation, related work references, and outbox before returning disposition.
Update/delete fails; correction appends and links; exact replay creates no duplicate; changed replay conflicts with no partial write.
Credentials, locators, capability/lease tokens, sensitive exact digests, and arbitrary bodies never enter public receipts or observability; protected reads are authorized and receipted.

Public safe summaries are server-generated from a closed structured schema; raw operator text is not copied by default; escaping, control-character handling, and token/credential/provider-locator redaction occur before public persistence/logging/tracing and hostile-content tests pass.
Outcome events reconcile to originating event, permit, message, and work references; unresolved routes remain queryable without claiming distributed atomicity.

Implementation evidence names the protected-evidence retention class, encrypted backup location, and restore-reader authorization and proves ordinary release/support backups exclude protected evidence, provider locators, permit bearers, lease receipts, and HMAC material.

Before full NAS production deployment, a dedicated read-only service identity and a distinct deny-by-default promotion writer are provisioned with server-side scoped permissions; exact names and secret provisioning are deployment-time fields, credentials are unavailable to agents, and use is auditable. A one-account design fails unless independent evidence proves separable server-side authorization without reusable write credential exposure.
Rollback occurs only under a protected Decision plus valid exact permit naming artifact/snapshot, target, trigger, action, key, and window; every mismatch yields zero mutation and a safe receipt.

No development agent credential, read-only service credential, Cable/Bishop/Bruce credential, or batman credential used by automation can deploy or roll back NAS; this does not narrow Sensei's direct human operator access.
